Senses.PreferredTarget: take away neither the person nor the surroundings
AlternateTargets: neither person nor surroundings taken away
Senses.Explanation: The fourth member of Linji's four statements later called the Four Selections: ‘at times, take away neither the person nor the surroundings.’ In Linji's own record it appears as one member of the complete four and immediately becomes a public question. Asked ‘what is taking away neither person nor surroundings?’ Linji answers, ‘the king ascends the jeweled hall; the rustic elder sings.’ The record does not explain the formula beyond that exchange. Later collections preserve Linji's wording, attach Kefu's verse—beginning ‘thought does not incline to either side; guest and host differ little; question and answer are both complete’—and invite many later masters to answer the same named question with new lines, including Fengxue's ‘the emperor remembers: in the third month south of the river, amid the partridge's cry the hundred flowers are fragrant.’ The formula circulates as a case heading, verse heading, and recurring public-interview question.
Senses.Note: 350 hits in the wave plan; preflight count retained by root. This formula must be read beside the other three members and the Four Selections (四料揀). Person (人) and surroundings (境) are translated literally here. It is corpus-wide in later use: later answers and verses address the same named formula rather than different things.

Senses.PreferredTarget: take away both person and scene
AlternateTargets: both person and surroundings taken away
Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘person and scene both taken away.’ The phrase occurs 168 times in 99 allowlisted texts. Linji lists it as the third of four alternatives: sometimes take away the person but not the scene; sometimes the scene but not the person; sometimes both; sometimes neither. The records preserve Kefu's answer to ‘what is taking away both person and scene?’ as ‘news from Bing and Fen is cut off; alone in one quarter.’ Later masters repeatedly submit the roster-member to fresh public questions: one answers ‘gather in,’ paired with ‘let out’ for taking away neither; another declines the inherited four choices and asks for a sentence in which person and scene are not taken away. The entry reports the roster and its recorded answers without assigning a hidden condition to ‘person’ or ‘scene.’
Senses.Note: Zen bends ordinary removal language into one named member of Linji's fourfold roster. It is a roster term and public-interview prompt, not a report that two physical objects disappeared. Cross-checking the other three members supports one sense, not four readings of this member.

Senses.Explanation: (殺人刀) = literally "the knife/sword that kills people." In the record it runs as a fixed pair with "the life-giving blade / the sword that brings people to life" (活人劍): (殺人刀) 399× in 142 allowlist files, (活人劍) 259× in 99, the two contiguous as (殺人刀活人劍) 23× in 12 files and paired within a single phrase 181× in 84. (圜悟克勤) opens Biyanlu pointers with the pair: "Pointer: the killing sword and the life-giving blade — this is the standard of high antiquity" (垂示云。殺人刀活人劍。乃上古之風規). His record continues "as for the killing sword, it leaves not a hair's breadth [standing]; the life-giving blade — corpses strewn for ten thousand li; know that within killing there is bringing-to-life, capturing and releasing humans and devas; within bringing-to-life there is killing, weighing buddhas and ancestors" (若論殺人刀不存毫末。活人劍橫屍萬里。須知殺中有活擒縱人天。活中有殺權衡佛祖). Another record states the reversal outright: (有時殺人刀即活人劍)，(有時活人劍即殺人刀) (J34nB311). Masters are measured against the pair: (天隱圓修) raises the old gauge "Shishuang had the killing sword but not the life-giving blade; Yantou had both" (石霜雖有殺人刀且無活人劍；巖頭亦有殺人刀亦有活人劍) and presses "now say — what is the killing sword, the life-giving blade?" (且道如何是殺人刀、活人劍？). It is likewise posed as a test question — (如何是殺人刀) 26× in 21 allowlist files — with recorded answers: 「(如何是殺人刀)？」(師打云)：「(一棒打殺)。」 (J10nA158); 「(如何是殺人刀)？」(師云)：「(與汝一頓)。」「(如何是活人劍)？」the master said: 'I want you to leap' (師云。要你𨁝跳). (J26nB178); and in (宏智覺禪師語錄), 「(如何是活人劍)？」(師曰)：「(放行瓦礫生光)。」「(如何是殺人刀)？」(師曰)：「(把定乾坤失色)。」 (J32nB272) — the pair answered with "letting go" (放行) and "holding fast" (把定). The texts deploy the pair in pointers, (示眾), and test questions without assigning it a gloss, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: The (殺)/(活) pair spans houses: (圜悟克勤) (Biyanlu T48n2003 + 圓悟語錄 T47n1997) and (天隱圓修) (J25nB171) in the Linji line, and the Caodong-line (宏智覺禪師語錄) (J32nB272), where (殺人刀)/(活人劍) are answered with (把定乾坤失色)/(放行瓦礫生光) — the texts' own pairing of the two swords with (把定) and (放行). (活人劍) co-occurs across ~100 allowlist texts, so the dyad is a shared Song-Chan trope, not one master's coinage. In-text co-phrasings: (殺中有活)/(活中有殺) (8× in 7 files, e.g. T47n1997's 擒縱人天/權衡佛祖 continuation) and (有時殺人刀即活人劍)，(有時活人劍即殺人刀) (J34nB311).

AlternateTargets: to kill and to give life
Senses.Explanation: A pair made from 'kill' (殺) and 'keep alive or give life' (活): killing and giving life. It appears with other paired Linji-house terms in the list 'killing and giving life, granting and taking, provisional and actual, illuminating and functioning' (殺活縱奪、權實照用). Fixed forms include 'free in killing and giving life' (殺活自在, 45 occurrences), 'killing or giving life according to the occasion' (殺活臨時), and 'killing and giving life at the same time or at different times' (殺活同時／殺活不同時). The record explicitly pairs it with the sword that kills a person (殺人刀) and the sword that gives a person life (活人劍): one turning word is the killing sword, one the life-giving sword, one kills and gives life at once, and one does so at different times (一轉語是殺人刀、一轉語是活人劍、一轉語殺活同時、一轉語殺活不同時). Another passage asks directly, 'What is killing?' (敢問如何是殺), and records the master's response of raising a foot. The headword occurs 1,275 times in 280 allowlisted texts, overwhelmingly in expositions and formula lists in later recorded sayings and lamp records.
Senses.Note: Corpus-wide vocabulary used especially in Linji-house descriptions, not a private coinage of one speaker. The curated passages are formula lists, a raised exchange, a proclamation, and preface prose, so their MasterName fields remain null. Compare the killing sword (殺人刀), the life-giving sword (活人劍), and the parallel pair 'illuminating and functioning' (照用).

Record of Guiding Principles from the Patriarchs (列祖提綱錄), in an imperial proclamation (受勅奉旨提綱). The sword image appears with 'killing or giving life according to the occasion' (如王寶劍，殺活臨時), immediately after the order to harbor no intellectual understanding (莫存知解).
